# Remote Deck
**SSH workspaces for DeepSeek Harness — one window, local and remote conversations side by side.**

Remote Deck connects your DSH desktop app to any number of SSH machines and turns a remote
folder in

to an ordinary DSH workspace. Inside that workspace the agent reads, writes, searches,
runs commands

, opens a terminal and forwards ports on the remote host — while the UI stays the
same window you al

terminal and forwards ports on the remote host — while the UI stays the
same window you already use.

- **Conversation first.** A compact status chip, a few badges, and a console that only appears
when

you open it. Nothing competes with the chat.
- **Many machines at once.** Every host has a colour id

entity, its own connection, and its own
group of workspaces and sessions.
- **No agent on the server

.** Only `sshd`: SFTP for files, exec channels for commands and search,
a PTY for the terminal, `dir
ect-tcpip` for port forwarding.
## Screens
| Console | Quick panel |
| Session identity | Add a machine |
| New workspace | Terminal and ports |

Screenshots are rendered from the sanitized design mockups in `docs/design/v2/`. Host names,
address
es and paths are demo data (`dev-box`, `203.0.113.10`, `/srv/demo-app`).
## Features
| Area | What you get |
| Connections | Multiple hosts, key or password auth, `~/.ssh/config` import, connection test with O
S/latency, per-host auto-connect (off by default; toggle in the dialog, quick panel or console), kee

palive and backoff reconnect |
| Workspaces | Browse remote folders with breadcrumbs, filters and ke
yboard navigation; add one as a DSH workspace; custom sidebar name; remove locally without touching

the remote directory |
| Sessions | Remote sessions get a header pill, a colour-coded sidebar badge

and a hover line; local sessions are unchanged |
| Console | Machine rail, host overview, stats, wor
kspace cards, recent sessions, search, and a remote file browser with download / save-to-local / rev

eal |
| Terminal | Remote PTY in a full xterm.js terminal: colours, cursor, full-screen programs, pa

ste and replay buffer |
| Ports | Automatic discovery of remote listening ports, one-click forwardin

g, persistence and restore on reconnect |
| Theme | Light and dark, driven by DSH theme tokens |

Restart DSH (or press `Ctrl+R`) after installing; the SSH chip appears at the bottom of the
sidebar
and **远程开发** appears in the sidebar navigation.

The plugin has **no npm dependencies**: `ssh2` and its small dependency tree are vendored under
`ven

dor/node_modules`, and the terminal assets under `vendor/xterm`. Installation therefore never
runs p
ackage build scripts.
## Migrating from `dsh-remote-ssh`
Remote Deck is the successor of `dsh-remote-ssh`.

- On first load it copies connections from `<DSH_HOME>/remote-ssh` and **reuses existing workspace
s

tubs in place**, so workspaces and sessions keep their place in the sidebar.
- The old plugin keeps

working until you remove it. Use one profile at a time: both plugins patch
`ctx.fs`, so only one of

them should be enabled in a profile.
- Cut over in one command (backs up `package.json` first and ke

eps the old plugin files for
rollback):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- Roll back at any time:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Data stays in `<DSH_HOME>/remote-deck` and survives plugin reinstalls.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A remote workspace is a marked stub directory under `<DSH_HOME>/remote-deck/workspaces`; the
marker

records the connection id and the remote POSIX path. Every path under a marked workspace
resolves th

rough SFTP; commands run through an exec channel with the remote cwd; ripgrep moves to
the host; the
terminal is one PTY channel; forwarding is one local listener per port.
## Security

- Passwords and key passphrases live in the DSH credential store, never in `connections.json`.
- The

browser half talks to the host over a loopback HTTP server guarded by a per-session token.
- The te

rminal and forwarding endpoints are behind the same token.
- Removing a workspace only unregisters i
t locally; remote files are never deleted by the plugin.
## Requirements
remote shell `bash`.
## Known limits

- The terminal ships a vendored xterm.js build (colours, cursor, full-screen programs). If the
asset

loader is blocked, the plugin falls back to a plain line renderer.
- The UI is Chinese-first; Engli

sh strings land in v1.1.0.
- `~/.ssh/config` import covers Host/HostName/Port/User/IdentityFile/Prox

yJump; proxy commands and
host-key pinning are not wired into the connection dialogs yet.
- `ss` or
`netstat` is required for automatic port discovery; manual forwarding still works.

unbook in docs/MAINTENANCE.md.
